world.title: Hegseth vows to fight impeachment as Democrats target Iran war
world.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth vowed Thursday to resist impeachment and defended the Iran war as “courageous and historic” after Republicans’ Nov. 3 midterm defeat put Democrats on track to take control of both chambers of Congress in January. Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky says he will press for a Hous
world.content: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth vowed Thursday to resist impeachment and defended the Iran war as “courageous and historic” after Republicans’ Nov. 3 midterm defeat put Democrats on track to take control of both chambers of Congress in January. Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky says he will press for a House vote when lawmakers return next week unless Hegseth resigns. Vice President JD Vance blamed the war for the Republican losses, while President Donald Trump agreed it contributed to the losses but defended the decision to attack Iran. Iran’s partial blockage of the Strait of Hormuz has disrupted the global economy and pushed energy prices higher, adding to voter frustration. Trump has publicly praised Hegseth, though reports say he has privately discussed the defense secretary’s future with aides. Democrats say they plan to investigate the war and Pentagon leadership when they take control in January; Massie plans to press for a House vote when Congress reconvenes on Nov. 9.
world.image_alt: Hegseth vows to fight impeachment as Democrats target Iran war

world.title: Pope Leo begins 12-day South American tour weeks after cancer surgery
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV left Rome on Friday, Nov. 6, for a 12-day visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, three weeks after surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his right lung. His doctors said the disease was localized and required no further treatment; the Vatican said he was cleared to travel without additional medical preca
world.content: Pope Leo XIV left Rome on Friday, Nov. 6, for a 12-day visit to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, three weeks after surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his right lung. His doctors said the disease was localized and required no further treatment; the Vatican said he was cleared to travel without additional medical precautions. The itinerary covers 10 cities and about 31,000 kilometers, with roughly 36 speeches. The first U.S.-born pope is returning to a region where he spent nearly two decades as a missionary, including in Peru, where he became a citizen. He is scheduled to meet the presidents of all three countries, celebrate outdoor Masses, visit an Argentine prison and travel to Andean and Amazonian communities. The Vatican says his speeches will address environmental destruction, arms trafficking and political instability; he will also meet survivors of clerical sexual abuse. Catholic affiliation has fallen in parts of the region, where the Church faces competition from evangelical denominations. Leo’s tour runs through Nov. 17, with six days scheduled in Peru, including visits to his former diocese of Chiclayo and the high-altitude city of Cusco.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo begins 12-day South American tour weeks after cancer surgery

world.title: Macau jails former lawmaker for 12½ years in first security trial
world.summary: A Macau court sentenced former pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam San to 12 years and six months in prison on Friday in the territory’s first national security trial. The 69-year-old was convicted of subversion, establishing links with groups outside Macau to endanger national security, and breaching confidentiality. The co
world.content: A Macau court sentenced former pro-democracy lawmaker Au Kam San to 12 years and six months in prison on Friday in the territory’s first national security trial. The 69-year-old was convicted of subversion, establishing links with groups outside Macau to endanger national security, and breaching confidentiality. The court acquitted him of two other subversion counts, citing insufficient evidence. Prosecutors said Au collaborated with overseas organizations in 2023 and 2024 to spread information they described as false or distorted and prompt hostile actions against China and Macau. The court also found that he disclosed confidential material from a 2021 legislative committee meeting on gaming-license renewals. His three-day trial took place behind closed doors in September. The court said it had approved regular prison visits for his family.
world.image_alt: Macau jails former lawmaker for 12½ years in first security trial

world.title: Iran reports five tankers and tugboat burned in Hormuz
world.summary: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and army said five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents in and near the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, with several vessels said to have struck naval mines. Maritime authorities had not independently confirmed the reported fires. Separately, the British maritime monitor
world.content: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards and army said five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents in and near the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, with several vessels said to have struck naval mines. Maritime authorities had not independently confirmed the reported fires. Separately, the British maritime monitor UKMTO reported that two unidentified projectiles struck a tanker off Qatar. The strait carried about one-fifth of global oil consumption before the war began in late February. Iran says vessels must coordinate passage with Tehran, while the United States has blockaded Iranian ports and helped tankers pass through the strait. President Donald Trump’s administration was weighing its next move after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections. Trump defended the war as necessary to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Iranian officials and Qatari mediators continued discussing proposals to end the conflict, but the sides remained far apart on the strait, sanctions, the U.S. blockade and nuclear negotiations.
world.image_alt: Iran reports five tankers and tugboat burned in Hormuz

world.title: Democrats win both chambers of Congress in setback for Trump
world.summary: Democrats won control of the U.S. House and Senate in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, ending the Republican Party’s hold on both chambers and delivering a setback to President Donald Trump. Preliminary results put Democrats at 54 Senate seats and at least 240 House seats, with Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi still
world.content: Democrats won control of the U.S. House and Senate in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, ending the Republican Party’s hold on both chambers and delivering a setback to President Donald Trump. Preliminary results put Democrats at 54 Senate seats and at least 240 House seats, with Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi still unresolved in reports published Thursday. The vote followed voter anger over living costs and fuel prices; Trump acknowledged that the Iran war had pushed gasoline costs higher. When the new Congress takes office on Jan. 3, 2027, Democrats will control committees and can investigate the administration, shape legislation and block or delay nominees who require Senate confirmation. Trump retains veto power, and analysts say Congress has limited ability to restrain a president’s use of military force abroad. Democrats say they will prioritize affordability and accountability, while Trump has threatened to veto legislation he opposes. Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican defeat, while Trump said he would launch the campaign again to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Democrats have also signaled investigations into Trump’s administration, family and allies, including the administration’s deportation policies and handling of files related to Jeffrey Epstein.
world.image_alt: Democrats win both chambers of Congress in setback for Trump

world.title: Stock selloff erases $2.5 trillion as AI policy fears hit markets
world.summary: U.S. technology shares plunged on Thursday, Nov. 5, wiping an estimated $2.5 trillion from the Nasdaq Composite as investors weighed the risk that Democrats’ midterm victories could slow artificial-intelligence data-center construction and tighten oversight. The Nasdaq fell 5.52%, its steepest daily percentage drop sin
world.content: U.S. technology shares plunged on Thursday, Nov. 5, wiping an estimated $2.5 trillion from the Nasdaq Composite as investors weighed the risk that Democrats’ midterm victories could slow artificial-intelligence data-center construction and tighten oversight. The Nasdaq fell 5.52%, its steepest daily percentage drop since April 2025, while the S&P 500 lost 4.36% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 3.44%. The selloff reversed a rally after Tuesday’s election and spread overseas on Friday: South Korea’s Kospi fell as much as 8.5%, triggering a 20-minute trading halt, while technology stocks in Japan and Taiwan also dropped sharply. Investors were already questioning whether heavy spending on AI infrastructure would generate adequate returns. The election added political risk, as winning candidates had campaigned against data centers over electricity use, water consumption and local impacts. The losses spread across chipmakers, data-center operators, cloud-computing firms and power and equipment suppliers, while President Donald Trump blamed Democrats for the market drop. The newly elected Congress takes office in January 2027, and investors are watching for policy proposals and local permitting decisions that could affect projects. Investors were also due to assess the U.S. October jobs report on Friday, Nov. 6.
world.image_alt: Stock selloff erases $2.5 trillion as AI policy fears hit markets

world.title: British comedian Russell Brand convicted of rape and three sexual assaults
world.summary: A London jury on Nov. 5 convicted British comedian and actor Russell Brand, 51, of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women, while acquitting him of two other rape charges and attempted indecent assault. Judge Joel Bennathan denied bail, remanded Brand in custody and said he faces a sig
world.content: A London jury on Nov. 5 convicted British comedian and actor Russell Brand, 51, of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women, while acquitting him of two other rape charges and attempted indecent assault. Judge Joel Bennathan denied bail, remanded Brand in custody and said he faces a significant prison term. Sentencing is scheduled for Monday, Nov. 9. The convictions concern a 2004 assault at a Soho bar, an assault on a radio-station worker in 2004 or 2005, an assault on a Channel 4 worker during a 2009 project, and the rape of a woman at Brand’s London home in 2009. The case involved six complainants and alleged offences spanning 1999 to 2009. British law protects the identities of people reporting sexual violence. Brand denied the charges and told the court the sexual encounters were consensual. His lawyers argued that the complainants’ delayed reports and a 2023 media investigation undermined the allegations; prosecutors said he had used his celebrity status to exploit women. Separately, London’s Metropolitan Police say they have sent files on two further rape allegations to prosecutors and are continuing their inquiries.
world.image_alt: British comedian Russell Brand convicted of rape and three sexual assaults

world.title: Eisenkot wins 67 endorsements, but Israeli coalition remains uncertain
world.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Nov. 8 which lawmaker he will ask to form a government. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot received recommendations from 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Oct. 27 election left neither political camp with
world.content: Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he will announce on Nov. 8 which lawmaker he will ask to form a government. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot received recommendations from 67 members of the 120-seat Knesset, compared with 46 for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Oct. 27 election left neither political camp with a governing majority; Herzog has said the recommendation tally does not determine who can assemble a workable coalition. Netanyahu’s Likud-led bloc holds 53 seats, while the Jewish-led opposition parties have 48. The Arab-led Joint List and Ra’am won 19 seats combined, and both recommended Eisenkot. United Torah Judaism, a seven-seat ultra-Orthodox party and Netanyahu ally, declined to endorse either candidate, leaving him with 46 recommendations. Some of Eisenkot’s prospective coalition partners reject cooperation with Arab parties, while Arab leaders have raised conditions and concerns of their own. The candidate Herzog designates will have 28 days to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension. Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister until a successor government is formed.
world.image_alt: Eisenkot wins 67 endorsements, but Israeli coalition remains uncertain

business.title: Anthropic investors question $1.5 trillion IPO price after tech selloff
business.summary: Investors preparing to back Anthropic’s planned initial public offering are questioning whether the artificial intelligence company can command its targeted $1.5 trillion valuation after a sharp selloff in technology shares. One investor believes the valuation may be closer to $1 trillion, while others have raised the
business.content: Investors preparing to back Anthropic’s planned initial public offering are questioning whether the artificial intelligence company can command its targeted $1.5 trillion valuation after a sharp selloff in technology shares. One investor believes the valuation may be closer to $1 trillion, while others have raised the possibility of reducing the offering’s size or delaying it. Anthropic had been targeting a roadshow the week of Nov. 9 and a listing before Thanksgiving, with plans to raise as much as $100 billion; the company has not publicly changed its timetable. The Nasdaq Composite lost about $2.5 trillion in market value in Thursday’s selloff as investors reassessed AI-related bets and concerns grew that political opposition could slow U.S. data-center construction. Anthropic executives and advisers are expected to review the IPO plans in the coming days. Investors are also weighing the company’s losses, infrastructure spending commitments and undisclosed October revenue figure before deciding what price they would support.
business.image_alt: Anthropic investors question $1.5 trillion IPO price after tech selloff

business.title: Democratic midterm wins put tech firms’ AI expansion under scrutiny
business.summary: Democrats’ victories in the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections will give the party control of Congress and several state governments, putting technology companies that aligned with President Donald Trump under greater political scrutiny. Democratic lawmakers have called for AI executives to testify and said they would inves
business.content: Democrats’ victories in the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections will give the party control of Congress and several state governments, putting technology companies that aligned with President Donald Trump under greater political scrutiny. Democratic lawmakers have called for AI executives to testify and said they would investigate the industry; some incoming governors have also promised pauses in large data-center construction. The vote followed voter concerns about AI’s effects on jobs, data centers and the cost of living: an NBC News exit poll found 56% of voters considered AI and data centers a crucial or major factor in their congressional choice. Democrats are due to take control of both chambers on Jan. 3, 2027, but any legislation would face divisions within the party and President Trump’s veto. Market analyst Dan Ives estimated that 10% of 800 to 1,000 planned U.S. data centers may not be built.
business.image_alt: Democratic midterm wins put tech firms’ AI expansion under scrutiny

business.title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue to block California’s child-safety law
business.summary: Google, Meta and TikTok filed separate federal lawsuits on Wednesday seeking to stop California from enforcing a law that bars social media platforms from offering users under 16 features such as personalized feeds and autoplay. Assembly Bill 1709, signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom in September, is scheduled to take effect J
business.content: Google, Meta and TikTok filed separate federal lawsuits on Wednesday seeking to stop California from enforcing a law that bars social media platforms from offering users under 16 features such as personalized feeds and autoplay. Assembly Bill 1709, signed by Gov. Gavin Newsom in September, is scheduled to take effect Jan. 1, 2027. The companies argue the law violates the First Amendment by dictating how platforms curate and display content, and conflicts with federal Section 230 protections. California Attorney General Rob Bonta’s office said it is reviewing the cases and will defend the state’s child-safety laws. The companies filed the cases in federal courts in San Francisco, Los Angeles and San Jose, seeking to block the law before it takes effect.
business.image_alt: Google, Meta and TikTok sue to block California’s child-safety law

business.title: China blocks SoftBank
business.summary: China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), the state planner, has barred Japanese conglomerate SoftBank from acquiring Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB’s robotics business in China, putting the planned $5.4 billion transaction in jeopardy. ABB said Thursday that Chinese regulators had informed it of
business.content: China’s National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC), the state planner, has barred Japanese conglomerate SoftBank from acquiring Swiss-Swedish engineering group ABB’s robotics business in China, putting the planned $5.4 billion transaction in jeopardy. ABB said Thursday that Chinese regulators had informed it of the prohibition. The review focused on whether robotics data and intellectual property developed in China could be transferred overseas and used to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, according to people familiar with the process cited by the Financial Times. China is ABB Robotics’ largest market, and more than 90% of the robots it sells to Chinese customers are made locally. SoftBank is assessing whether to seek approval again, while the companies remain in discussions. The status of the transaction outside China has not been specified.

business.title: Singapore Airlines commits S$2 billion to long-haul cabin overhaul
business.summary: Singapore Airlines unveiled a cabin overhaul costing more than S$2 billion ($1.6 billion), covering 41 Airbus A350-900s and 31 Boeing 777-9s across its four travel classes. The airline plans to begin installing the cabins in the second half of 2027, with the programme expected to continue through 2030. The redesign add
business.content: Singapore Airlines unveiled a cabin overhaul costing more than S$2 billion ($1.6 billion), covering 41 Airbus A350-900s and 31 Boeing 777-9s across its four travel classes. The airline plans to begin installing the cabins in the second half of 2027, with the programme expected to continue through 2030. The redesign adds sliding privacy doors to business class and a first-class suite with adjoining seats that can convert into a double bed measuring 80 inches by 60 inches. Singapore Airlines is extending the programme to A350s because delays to the 777-9’s entry into service have left its delivery date uncertain; the new business-class seats are also awaiting certification for the A350. The airline says it is funding the investment from cash reserves. Air France, British Airways and United Airlines are also focusing on premium travel.
business.image_alt: Singapore Airlines commits S$2 billion to long-haul cabin overhaul

business.title: Paraguay bank collapse blocks deposits and strains retailers
business.summary: Paraguay’s importers and retailers warned that the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank could cut sales at major retailers by 35%, as millions of customers lost access to accounts and payments. The lender reported about 3 million customers and roughly $850 million in public funds, including state and pension-related mo
business.content: Paraguay’s importers and retailers warned that the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank could cut sales at major retailers by 35%, as millions of customers lost access to accounts and payments. The lender reported about 3 million customers and roughly $850 million in public funds, including state and pension-related money. Its failure also prompted President Santiago Peña to submit his resignation and triggered impeachment proceedings. The central bank is working to transfer customer accounts to other financial institutions, but the process contributed to outages on other banks’ apps. Ueno had also said it secured about $510 million in financing from development institutions, funds and capital markets, including a $350 million bond issue led by JPMorgan and Bank of America. Paraguay’s central bank began guarantee payments for eligible customers with balances up to 10 million guaraníes. The deposit-insurance cap is 228.3 million guaraníes per depositor at each financial institution.
business.image_alt: Paraguay bank collapse blocks deposits and strains retailers

business.title: Democrats win Congress on affordability pledge, face Trump veto barriers
business.summary: Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections after campaigning on lowering household costs. They now face pressure to deliver results while President Donald Trump remains in the White House. Their proposals include restoring health-insurance subsidies, reversing Medicaid cuts, roll
business.content: Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections after campaigning on lowering household costs. They now face pressure to deliver results while President Donald Trump remains in the White House. Their proposals include restoring health-insurance subsidies, reversing Medicaid cuts, rolling back tariffs and expanding housing supply. At least seven Republican-held Senate seats changed hands. Trump can veto legislation, and Democrats lack the two-thirds majorities needed to override him. Analysts say lawmakers could link an extension of Republican tax cuts to renewed health-insurance subsidies, but one forecast puts a deal no earlier than late 2027, with benefits arriving in 2028. Congress also faces a Dec. 11 deadline to fund the government, with another shutdown possible.
business.image_alt: Democrats win Congress on affordability pledge, face Trump veto barriers

business.title: Wendy
business.summary: Wendy’s rejected a $1.4 billion cash offer led by activist investor Nelson Peltz and adopted a one-year shareholder-rights plan to deter an unsolicited takeover. The investor group, which includes Trian Fund Management, Flynn Group, BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street Partners, offered $7.35 per share for stock it does n
business.content: Wendy’s rejected a $1.4 billion cash offer led by activist investor Nelson Peltz and adopted a one-year shareholder-rights plan to deter an unsolicited takeover. The investor group, which includes Trian Fund Management, Flynn Group, BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street Partners, offered $7.35 per share for stock it does not already own. Wendy’s independent directors said the proposal undervalued the company and its longer-term earnings potential. The defense can be triggered if an investor with at least 15% of shares buys more without board approval. The group already owns 16.3%, so the plan also covers additional purchases by existing holders above the threshold. Wendy’s is backing CEO Bob Wright’s Dave’s Way turnaround plan after U.S. same-store sales fell 5.7% in the third quarter. The rights plan took effect Nov. 4 and is scheduled to expire Nov. 3, 2027.

science.title: Ancient DNA studies trace Germanic, Celtic language migrations across Europe
science.summary: Two studies combining ancient DNA, archaeology and language trace migrations that may have helped spread Germanic and Celtic languages across Europe. The research, published in Nature, analyzed DNA from more than 4,500 ancient people, including 712 newly sequenced genomes. It identifies a previously unknown migration i
science.content: Two studies combining ancient DNA, archaeology and language trace migrations that may have helped spread Germanic and Celtic languages across Europe. The research, published in Nature, analyzed DNA from more than 4,500 ancient people, including 712 newly sequenced genomes. It identifies a previously unknown migration into Scandinavia from the Baltic region about 4,000 years ago, roughly 800 years later than an older theory dated the arrival of Germanic languages. A separate migration west from central Europe about 3,000 years ago offers an explanation for the spread of Celtic languages, challenging—but not ruling out—the theory of an Atlantic origin. The studies also identify migration from northern Germany into Denmark and southern Sweden about 1,500 years ago, around the emergence of Old Norse. Researchers stress that genetic ancestry cannot establish which language a person spoke, and that language can spread through contact without large-scale migration. The Celtic analysis likewise allows that contact helped carry the language west; it does not exclude the Atlantic-origin theory.
science.image_alt: Ancient DNA studies trace Germanic, Celtic language migrations across Europe

science.title: Archaeologists challenge claim that Iron Age ruler Verica was female
science.summary: Archaeologist Miles Russell of Bournemouth University argues that Verica, an Iron Age ruler of southern Britain whose exile preceded Rome’s invasion, was a woman. Oxford archaeologist Roger Tomlin and British Iron Age coin specialist Daphne Nash Briggs dispute his interpretation, which is based on Verica’s name, coins
science.content: Archaeologist Miles Russell of Bournemouth University argues that Verica, an Iron Age ruler of southern Britain whose exile preceded Rome’s invasion, was a woman. Oxford archaeologist Roger Tomlin and British Iron Age coin specialist Daphne Nash Briggs dispute his interpretation, which is based on Verica’s name, coins and inscriptions. The debate centers on whether the evidence establishes Verica’s sex: Russell interprets one coin as depicting a female rider and says inscriptions could mean “daughter of Commios,” while critics note that other coins show apparently male figures and question whether Rome used the title rex for women. Tomlin said the case needs stronger evidence that rex was used for women. Russell’s argument appears in Current Archaeology and in his book, Caratacus: Great King of Britain.
science.image_alt: Archaeologists challenge claim that Iron Age ruler Verica was female

science.title: New geological tests leave Stonehenge altar stone’s Scottish origin unconfirmed
science.summary: A new geological study found no exact match for Stonehenge’s six-tonne Altar Stone in the Orcadian Basin of northeast Scotland, leaving its source unresolved and weakening the leading Scottish-origin theory. The researchers say the stone may instead come from another part of Scotland, northern England or Ireland. They
science.content: A new geological study found no exact match for Stonehenge’s six-tonne Altar Stone in the Orcadian Basin of northeast Scotland, leaving its source unresolved and weakening the leading Scottish-origin theory. The researchers say the stone may instead come from another part of Scotland, northern England or Ireland. They ruled out southern Britain and previously proposed Welsh sources. The 4.9-metre sandstone slab was long thought to come from Wales, until a 2024 study pointed to northeast Scotland. The latest research compares the stone’s mineral, chemical and structural characteristics with those of possible source rocks, but does not identify a matching location. Study leader Professor Duncan Pirrie said the findings give researchers a clearer profile of the stone to guide further searches, though its exact origin remains unknown.
science.image_alt: New geological tests leave Stonehenge altar stone’s Scottish origin unconfirmed

science.title: Study shows endangered Hawaiian bird drills wood with whole body
science.summary: A study in the journal Ornithology finds that the endangered ʻakiapōlāʻau uses its legs and body momentum, along with its distinctive beak, to gouge wood for insect larvae. The bird chisels into branches with its short, heavy lower bill, then probes the opening for prey with its long, flexible upper bill. Researchers s
science.content: A study in the journal Ornithology finds that the endangered ʻakiapōlāʻau uses its legs and body momentum, along with its distinctive beak, to gouge wood for insect larvae. The bird chisels into branches with its short, heavy lower bill, then probes the opening for prey with its long, flexible upper bill. Researchers say the species fills a feeding role similar to that of woodpeckers, which are not native to Hawaii. Researchers examined museum specimens to identify the anatomy behind this behavior, including a strong ankle-flexing muscle that helps drive the bird downward. Fewer than 2,000 are thought to remain in the wild, all on one mountain slope on the island of Hawaii.
science.image_alt: Study shows endangered Hawaiian bird drills wood with whole body

science.title: Mars study links Alba Mons gas to possible underground magma
science.summary: A study published Nov. 4 links hydrogen chloride detected over Mars’ Alba Mons to narrow surface fissures and possible magma beneath them. The European Space Agency’s Trace Gas Orbiter measured the gas at parts-per-billion levels, including during a cold Martian season when researchers did not expect to detect it. Imag
science.content: A study published Nov. 4 links hydrogen chloride detected over Mars’ Alba Mons to narrow surface fissures and possible magma beneath them. The European Space Agency’s Trace Gas Orbiter measured the gas at parts-per-billion levels, including during a cold Martian season when researchers did not expect to detect it. Images show fractures in the same region. The researchers propose that the fissures allow gas to escape from underground and that winter ice could block them before sublimating in early summer. The interpretation is unconfirmed: University of Bern researcher Nicolas Thomas said ground-level investigation would be needed for unambiguous proof, and no new eruption or lava flow has been observed.
science.image_alt: Mars study links Alba Mons gas to possible underground magma

science.title: Study links Pacific garbage patch color shift to microplastics
science.summary: Researchers at the University of Bergen report that satellite records show brighter blue and green light in and around the Great Pacific Garbage Patch between 2002 and 2022, a pattern that may give the water a more cyan hue. Their study, published Nov. 5 in Communications Earth & Environment, suggests that accumulating
science.content: Researchers at the University of Bergen report that satellite records show brighter blue and green light in and around the Great Pacific Garbage Patch between 2002 and 2022, a pattern that may give the water a more cyan hue. Their study, published Nov. 5 in Communications Earth & Environment, suggests that accumulating microplastics could produce the change but does not establish that they caused it. The team tested how microplastics scatter light in the laboratory, then modeled their effects alongside natural influences such as phytoplankton. Adding plastics made the observed blue-and-green brightening more likely, but the satellite datasets differed in the size of the change, and some natural conditions can create a similar signal. The researchers say verifying the link requires collecting water samples in the patch, measuring their optical properties and quantifying the plastic. Such fieldwork would be difficult and costly. If validated, the method could help locate other plastic concentrations that are difficult to measure through labor-intensive sampling, though researchers say it would still need testing in different ocean environments.
science.image_alt: Study links Pacific garbage patch color shift to microplastics

science.title: Octopuses use different escape moves to squeeze through tight holes
science.summary: Experiments show that young common octopuses use different escape movements depending on whether an opening is wider or narrower than the distance between their eyes, a measure of the stiff cartilage around the brain. For wider holes, the animals thread several arms through, then brace against the wall to pull their he
science.content: Experiments show that young common octopuses use different escape movements depending on whether an opening is wider or narrower than the distance between their eyes, a measure of the stiff cartilage around the brain. For wider holes, the animals thread several arms through, then brace against the wall to pull their head, mantle and remaining arms through. At narrower holes, they send all their arms through first, then compress the mantle and pull the rest of the body through. The team tested three common octopuses and four Mayan octopuses in clear boxes with openings sized relative to each animal’s eye-to-eye distance. Mayan octopuses avoided the narrower opening, and the researchers cautioned that the small sample and unsuccessful attempts limit how broadly the results apply. The researchers say the movement strategies could inform soft-bodied search-and-rescue robots, which currently tend to use slender, snake-like designs.
science.image_alt: Octopuses use different escape moves to squeeze through tight holes

science.title: Blue Origin delays New Glenn return to January 2027 after pad blast
science.summary: Blue Origin, Jeff Bezos’ space company, has postponed its next New Glenn rocket launch from the end of this year to January 2027. CEO Dave Limp told employees that delays in rebuilding the launchpad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, partly caused by summer weather, forced the change. A May 28 explosion during a ho
science.content: Blue Origin, Jeff Bezos’ space company, has postponed its next New Glenn rocket launch from the end of this year to January 2027. CEO Dave Limp told employees that delays in rebuilding the launchpad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, partly caused by summer weather, forced the change. A May 28 explosion during a hot-fire test severely damaged the Florida launchpad shortly before a flight intended to deploy 48 satellites for Amazon’s Leo satellite-internet service. No injuries were reported. The delay has slowed Leo’s buildout, and Amazon has used other launch providers while Blue Origin repairs the site.
science.image_alt: Blue Origin delays New Glenn return to January 2027 after pad blast

sports.title: Jaguars beat Ravens to open NFL Week 9
sports.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday to open NFL Week 9, led by Trevor Lawrence’s passing. Lawrence averaged more than 9 yards per attempt, while Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Nate Boerkircher each had at least 60 receiving yards. Baltimore got little production from its leading running
sports.content: The Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Baltimore Ravens on Thursday to open NFL Week 9, led by Trevor Lawrence’s passing. Lawrence averaged more than 9 yards per attempt, while Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Nate Boerkircher each had at least 60 receiving yards. Baltimore got little production from its leading running backs, and safety Kyle Hamilton left with a hip injury. The remaining schedule includes Sunday’s Cincinnati Bengals-Atlanta Falcons game in Madrid and a Monday night meeting between the 6-1 Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings. Minnesota will start Carson Wentz at quarterback because Kyler Murray has a hamstring injury. Week 9 ends Monday, Nov. 9, a day before the NFL’s Nov. 10 trade deadline.
sports.image_alt: Jaguars beat Ravens to open NFL Week 9

sports.title: Van Dijk urges Liverpool to fix European defensive failures
sports.summary: Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk called his side’s Champions League defending “not sustainable” after a 3-2 loss to Fenerbahce in which Liverpool conceded three goals for the third European match in a row. He said the team switched off at set pieces and was not ready for the first and second balls; Fenerbahce scored f
sports.content: Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk called his side’s Champions League defending “not sustainable” after a 3-2 loss to Fenerbahce in which Liverpool conceded three goals for the third European match in a row. He said the team switched off at set pieces and was not ready for the first and second balls; Fenerbahce scored from a free-kick, a corner and a long throw. The run marks the first time Liverpool have conceded at least three goals in three consecutive major European matches. Liverpool won the previous two despite conceding three against LASK and Villarreal, but their defensive lapses proved decisive in Istanbul. Van Dijk said the squad must learn from back-to-back defeats before Liverpool travel to Crystal Palace on Sunday in the Premier League. The captain said the club must focus on improving, while head coach Andoni Iraola also acknowledged the need to defend better.

sports.content: Australian batter Chris Lynn served a one-month suspension after testing positive for a cocaine metabolite at England’s T20 Blast Finals Day in July, the Cricket Regulator disclosed on Nov. 5. Lynn said he used cocaine outside competition on July 15-16. The regulator accepted that the violation was unrelated to his cricket performance and reduced a proposed three-month ban after he completed a substance-abuse treatment program. The 36-year-old’s suspension ran from July 31 to Aug. 30, and Northamptonshire Steelbacks received no sanction. Lynn has been linked with a move to the Melbourne Renegades ahead of the Big Bash League season, which starts next month. If he joins, any additional disciplinary action would be at his new club’s discretion because he is not contracted to Cricket Australia.

sports.content: Rory McIlroy accepted a two-shot penalty after officials ruled he improved his lie on the 12th hole during Thursday’s opening round of the Abu Dhabi Championship at Yas Links. The ruling turned his double bogey into an eight, giving him a two-under-par 70 and leaving him eight shots behind leader Francesco Laporta. McIlroy said he had not intended to gain an advantage but accepted the penalty after reviewing video, saying he did not want anyone to think he had “got away with something”. The tournament is the first of two season-ending Race to Dubai playoff events. McIlroy is pursuing an eighth Race to Dubai title, while Spanish golfer Eugenio Chacarra leads the standings. Laporta opened with a 62 for a three-shot lead, and the second round is scheduled for Friday.

sports.content: Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel Alameda, 30, was buried Thursday in Navahermosa, Spain, after dying from injuries sustained in a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a second-division match on Monday. Hundreds attended the funeral, including de Miguel’s teammates and senior figures from Spanish football. His family thanked mourners and asked for privacy as they grieve. The Spanish footballers’ union AFE called for all matches this weekend to be postponed, saying players did not feel able to compete normally. LaLiga decided fixtures would go ahead except those involving Tenerife, Andorra and de Miguel’s former club Castellón. Tenerife plans a public tribute at its stadium on Saturday, November 7.

sports.summary: The Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) apologized Thursday after a courtside microphone broadcast American Jessica Pegula’s private criticism of Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva during a practice livestream at Indian Wells, California, ahead of the season-ending WTA Finals. The fifth-ranked Pegula called Andreeva, the 19-
sports.content: The Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) apologized Thursday after a courtside microphone broadcast American Jessica Pegula’s private criticism of Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva during a practice livestream at Indian Wells, California, ahead of the season-ending WTA Finals. The fifth-ranked Pegula called Andreeva, the 19-year-old French Open champion ranked third, “a diva” and said she needed to be humbled. Pegula also criticized Andreeva’s coach, Conchita Martinez. The WTA said it had failed to tell players and coaches that microphones were active. It removed the practice recordings, but clips had already spread online. Pegula’s representative said she had not known the conversation was being broadcast and had contacted those involved. The microphones were meant to capture court sounds; future practice streams will have no audio. Pegula and Andreeva are in separate groups and could meet only in the semifinals or final. The tournament runs through Nov. 15.

sports.title: Deschamps reluctant to take Manchester United job as Carrick faces scrutiny

sports.content: Manchester United have sounded out former France coach Didier Deschamps about replacing head coach Michael Carrick, but reports say the World Cup-winning manager is reluctant to take the job and is in no hurry to return to management. Foot Mercato’s account, carried by Football360, says United made an initial approach, but neither a formal offer nor a definitive rejection has been confirmed. Carrick remains under pressure after United won only once in their first nine Premier League matches and fell to 17th place. A 3-2 comeback win against Roma in the Champions League ended a nine-game winless run. United host Aston Villa on Sunday, and the club’s leadership could review Carrick’s position during the November international break. Deschamps left the France job after the 2026 World Cup, ending a 14-year spell that included the 2018 world title. He has not managed a club since leaving Marseille in 2012. Reports say his concerns include United’s instability, fan discontent and recruitment; he may wait until the next summer transfer window for a project that appeals to him.

sports.title: Jaguars beat Ravens 33-10 as rookie quarterback Fagnano throws two interceptions
sports.summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 in Baltimore on Thursday, Nov. 5, earning their fifth victory in six games and improving to 6-2. The Ravens fell to 4-5 with their fourth straight defeat. Jacksonville took control with a 77-yard opening drive and a 50-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Trevor
sports.content: The Jacksonville Jaguars beat the Baltimore Ravens 33-10 in Baltimore on Thursday, Nov. 5, earning their fifth victory in six games and improving to 6-2. The Ravens fell to 4-5 with their fourth straight defeat. Jacksonville took control with a 77-yard opening drive and a 50-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Trevor Lawrence to Parker Washington late in the first half. Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown, while Baltimore rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw for 60 yards and two interceptions in his first NFL start. The Jaguars’ defense held the Ravens to 227 total yards and forced three turnovers. Baltimore’s only touchdown came on Justice Hill’s 65-yard run late in the game. Jacksonville strengthened its hold on the AFC South, while the Ravens await veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett’s arrival in a trade from Arizona. Baltimore next plays the Los Angeles Chargers on Nov. 16, after which Brissett could take over at quarterback.
